title: Tarik Skubal Tops MLB Trade Market as Tigers Face Pivotal Deadline Decision
excerpt: ESPN gives the two-time Cy Young winner a 60% chance of being traded before August 3, but Detroit's recent surge and Skubal's own preference to stay complicate what could be the summer's biggest deal.
body:
The 2026 MLB trade deadline is 12 days away, and every conversation about it starts and ends with the same name: Tarik Skubal.

ESPN's Jeff Passan and Kiley McDaniel released their updated top-100 trade candidate rankings on Tuesday, placing the Detroit Tigers left-hander at the top of the list with a 60% chance of being dealt. "Considering the hole they've dug themselves, they are far more likely than not to move Skubal," the ESPN analysts wrote. "He is the dream deadline candidate, the sort of ace who can carry a team in the postseason. Whoever lands Skubal will pay an enormous price. Happily."

A seller's market with almost no sellers

What makes the 2026 deadline landscape unusual is how few teams are truly ready to sell. At the start of play Tuesday, 19 of 30 MLB clubs carried consensus postseason odds of 15% or greater, according to projections from Baseball-Reference, FanGraphs, and PECOTA. The clear sellers — the Mets, Rockies, Angels, Athletics, Nationals, and Giants — are a short list, and most of them lack a franchise-altering trade chip.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=kmsSKp6mAuM

That puts an enormous premium on Skubal, the 29-year-old who has won back-to-back AL Cy Young Awards and sits on an expiring contract. If he reaches free agency after this season, the Tigers get nothing in return. Trading him now could reshape the franchise for years.

"Considering the hole they've dug themselves, they are far more likely than not to move Skubal. He is the dream deadline candidate."

— ESPN's Jeff Passan and Kiley McDaniel

The Tigers' dilemma: contend or cash in

Here is what makes this particular decision so agonizing for Detroit. The Tigers are not dead. At 47-53, they trail the final AL wild-card spot by 4.5 games and the AL Central-leading Cleveland Guardians by 6.5 games. Since June 1, Detroit has played at a 24-15 clip — the kind of surge that turns fringe contenders into October participants.

Skubal has been vocal about his desire for the Tigers to add rather than subtract at the deadline. USA Today's Bob Nightengale, bucking the consensus, predicted that Skubal stays in Detroit. "Skubal, the defending two-time AL Cy Young winner, realizes his fate depends on how the Tigers fare these next weeks," Nightengale wrote. "If they keep winning — and they're 24-15 since June 1 — he's staying. Prediction: Staying."

The Tigers have 12 games before the August 3 deadline to settle the question. A winning stretch could justify holding their ace for a playoff push. A stumble would make the case for cashing in overwhelming.

Half the league wants him

The line of suitors runs deep. Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller identified the Atlanta Braves and Los Angeles Dodgers as the two most logical landing spots, with Atlanta needing a second postseason-caliber starter alongside Chris Sale, and the Dodgers dealing with injuries to Shohei Ohtani (knee), Tyler Glasnow (back), and Blake Snell (elbow).

The Chicago Cubs, with an 83.5% postseason probability but a rotation decimated by the losses of Cade Horton (UCL surgery) and Justin Steele (still sidelined), would need to assemble a massive prospect package. The Milwaukee Brewers, owners of the best record in baseball, have already added Lance McCullers Jr. from Houston and could go bigger for Skubal given their loaded farm system. The Tampa Bay Rays, leading the AL wild-card race at 96.3% playoff odds, have also been named among the teams pushing hardest for a deal.

The Athletic's Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal reported the contours of Detroit's asking price: a controllable young starting pitcher plus quality prospects. They identified several arms that could anchor such a package, including Tampa Bay's Ian Seymour, Philadelphia's Andrew Painter, the Dodgers' Emmet Sheehan, and Milwaukee's Logan Henderson.

Detroit's trade stockpile runs deep

Skubal is the headline, but the Tigers have a roster full of expiring contracts that make them a potential one-stop deadline shop. Casey Mize, the former No. 1 overall pick, ranks 16th on ESPN's trade list. Despite two stints on the injured list with groin issues, Mize has been outstanding when healthy, posting a 2.62 FIP and 2.8 FanGraphs WAR.

Gleyber Torres (No. 43 on the ESPN list) has slashed .288/.405/.400 and brings seven postseasons of experience, including six with the New York Yankees. Right-hander Jack Flaherty (No. 46), who was traded by Detroit to the Dodgers at the 2024 deadline and later returned on a two-year deal, has put up a 2.18 ERA across his last four starts. Even closer Kenley Jansen and reliever Drew Anderson appear on the list, giving contenders multiple entry points for a deal with Detroit.

"If they keep winning — and they're 24-15 since June 1 — he's staying. Prediction: Staying."

— USA Today's Bob Nightengale on Tarik Skubal

What's next

The next two weeks will determine whether the Tigers become the deadline's biggest sellers or defy expectations and hold their ace for an October run. Detroit plays at the Cubs through Thursday before returning home to face the Guardians — a stretch that could tip the scales decisively in one direction.

If the Tigers falter, expect a bidding war that could produce one of the largest prospect hauls in recent deadline history. If they keep winning, the story of the 2026 trade deadline may be the deal that never happened.
